arxiv-2107-11781.title: Towards Controlled and Diverse Generation of Article Comments
arxiv-2107-11781.creator: Linhao Zhang, Houfeng Wang
arxiv-2107-11781.description: A 2021 arXiv research paper by Linhao Zhang, Houfeng Wang. Much research in recent years has focused on automatic article commenting. However, few of previous studies focus on the controllable generation of comments. Besides, they tend to generate dull and commonplace comments, which further limits their practical application. In this paper, we make the first step towards controllable generation of comments, by building a system that can explicitly control the emotion of the generated comments.

arxiv-2203-11016.title: Linking Theories and Methods in Cognitive Sciences via Joint Embedding of the Scientific Literature: The Example of Cognitive Control
arxiv-2203-11016.creator: Morteza Ansarinia, Paul Schrater, Pedro Cardoso-Leite
arxiv-2203-11016.description: Abstract Traditionally, theory and practice of Cognitive Control are linked via literature reviews by human domain experts. This approach, however, is inadequate to track the ever-growing literature. It may also be biased, and yield redundancies and confusion. Here we present an alternative approach.

arxiv-2502-12204.title: Predicting Depression in Screening Interviews from Interactive Multi-Theme Collaboration
arxiv-2502-12204.creator: Xianbing Zhao, Yiqing Lyu, Di Wang, Buzhou Tang
arxiv-2502-12204.description: Abstract Automatic depression detection provides cues for early clinical intervention by clinicians. Clinical interviews for depression detection involve dialogues centered around multiple themes. Existing studies primarily design end-to-end neural network models to capture the hierarchical structure of clinical interview dialogues.

arxiv-2504-04054.title: SageNet: Fast Neural Network Emulation of the Stiff-amplified Gravitational Waves from Inflation SageNet ( https://github.com/YifangLuo/SageNet ), stiffGWpy ( https://github.com/bohuarolandli/stiffGWpy ), PyTorch ( A. Paszke et al. 2019 )
arxiv-2504-04054.creator: Fan Zhang, Yifang Luo, Bohua Li, Ruihan Cao, Wenjin Peng, Joel Meyers, Paul R. Shapiro
arxiv-2504-04054.description: Abstract Accurate modeling of the inflationary gravitational waves (GWs) requires time-consuming, iterative numerical integrations of differential equations to take into account their backreaction on the expansion history. To improve computational efficiency while preserving accuracy, we present SageNet (Stiff-Amplified Gravitational-wave Emulator Network), a deep learning framework designed to replace conventional numerical solvers 1 1 1 Code available at: https://github.com/YifangLuo/SageNet .

arxiv-2506-00430.title: MIRROR: Cognitive Inner Monologue Between Conversational Turns for Persistent Reflection and Reasoning in Conversational LLMs
arxiv-2506-00430.creator: Nicole S. Hsing
arxiv-2506-00430.description: Abstract Human intelligence relies on inner monologue to process complex information through simultaneous reflection, memory retrieval, and response formulation. We introduce MIRROR (Modular Internal Reasoning, Reflection, Orchestration, and Response), a cognitive architecture that systematically implements these parallel reasoning capabilities in large language models. MIRROR operates as a unified system with two distinct functional layers: the Thinker and the Talker.

arxiv-2506-03138.title: Change of bifurcation type in 2D free boundary model of a moving cell with nonlinear diffusion
arxiv-2506-03138.creator: Leonid Berlyand, Oleksii Krupchytskyi, Tim Laux
arxiv-2506-03138.description: Abstract . We introduce a 2D free boundary problem with nonlinear diffusion that models a living cell moving on a substrate. We prove that this nonlinearity results in a qualitative change of solution behavior compared to the linear diffusion case (Rybalko et al. TAMS 2023), namely the switch between direct and inverse pitchfork bifurcation.

pmc-10634461.title: Hepatic Abscess in Inflammatory Bowel Disease: A Systematic Scoping Review of an Overlooked Entity
pmc-10634461.creator: Shadi Abdullah Alshammary, Dhuha Nahar Boumarah
pmc-10634461.description: Background:Liver abscess is one of the hepatobiliary manifestations of inflammatory bowel disease (IBD) that has been scarcely described in the literature.Objectives:To conduct a scoping review to provide a detailed description of the occurrence of hepatic abscess in patients with IBD and summarize the observed clinical features.

pmc-11678266.title: Anticancer Activity of Plant Tocotrienols, Fucoxanthin, Fucoidan, and Polyphenols in Dietary Supplements
pmc-11678266.creator: Gabriel Lara-Hernández, José Alberto Ramos-Silva, Elvia Pérez-Soto, Mario Figueroa, Ericka Patricia Flores-Berrios, Laura Sánchez-Chapul, José Luis Andrade-Cabrera, Alexandra Luna-Angulo, Carlos Landa-Solís, Hamlet Avilés-Arnaut
pmc-11678266.description: A peer-reviewed research article from Europe PMC (2024). Background: Plants and algae harbor diverse molecules with antioxidant activity and have been demonstrated to directly inhibit cancer cell growth and mitigate the oxidative damage associated with certain antitumor therapies. While antioxidant supplementation, either alone or in combination with chemotherapy, has shown promise in improving quality of life, further research is needed to explore the effects of antioxidant combinations on specific cancer cell lines.

pmc-12560522.title: Associations between reproductive factors and frailty in middle-aged and older women: evidence from the China health and retirement longitudinal study
pmc-12560522.creator: Xiaobing Xian, Jie Xiang, Shiwei Cao, Wanting Tang, Yao Wu, Jiaxia Li, Shiqin Ren, Yuanyuan Wang, Kun Shen
pmc-12560522.description: BackgroundAmid global aging, frailty significantly threatens the health of middle-aged and older women. This study is the first to explore the association between reproductive factors (age at first livebirth, number of biological children, reproductive period, age at menopause, age at menarche, and history of abortion) and frailty among middle-aged and elderly Chinese women.

pmc-12599557.title: Progress in the study of molecular markers in the prognosis assessment and recurrence patterns of glioblastoma
pmc-12599557.creator: Yuqing Hu, Xiaoqin Ge, Qianyun Xie, Ruishuang Ma, Qingsong Tao
pmc-12599557.description: Glioblastoma multiforme (GBM), the most invasive primary malignant tumor of the central nervous system, is characterized by an extremely poor prognosis and a high recurrence rate. Its significant molecular heterogeneity challenges precise diagnosis and treatment. Recently, with the rapid development of molecular pathology, the combination of histological and molecular typing has become the mainstream method for GBM diagnosis.

pmc-13145962.title: ABSTRACT NUMBER: ESOC2026A460 PLASMA PROTEOMIC PROFILES LINKED TO POST-STROKE MYOCARDIAL INJURY
pmc-13145962.creator: Helena Stengl, Markus Klammer, Simon Hellwig, Matthias Ziehm, Philipp Mertins, Monika Svecla, Ran Xu, Jan Scheitz
pmc-13145962.description: Background and aimsAcute myocardial injury after stroke is considered part of the spectrum of the stroke-heart syndrome and is strongly associated with unfavorable short-term outcomes. The aim of this study was to identify plasma proteomic changes among stroke patients with acute myocardial injury compared to those without.

pmc-13218345.title: Investigating the agronomic performance and ecological weed-suppression effects of summer leguminous green manure in dragon fruit orchards
pmc-13218345.creator: Shengjian Kuang, Heng Liao, Danjun Yao, Shan Yang, Qin Zhang, Song Qin, Yanfei Liang, Aihua Zhang
pmc-13218345.description: BackgroundThe large-scale cultivation of dragon fruit (Selenicereus undatus) in China faces challenges in sustainable weed management, particularly during the summer season. There is a notable lack of suitable green manure species for mountainous orchards that can effectively suppress weeds while enhancing ecological sustainability.

pmc-13242467.title: Conservation Planning and Reporting Implications of qPCR-based Multi-species eDNA Detection Under EU Environmental Regulations
pmc-13242467.creator: Simone Giovacchini, Enrico Mirone, Antonia Bruno, Fausto Ramazzotti, Luca Caprotti, Pamela Monaco, Mirko Di Febbraro, Chiara Manfrin, Pushpinder Singh Jamwal, Francesco Belluardo, Andrea Galimberti, Anna Loy
pmc-13242467.description: European Union (EU) legislation supports the conservation of endangered freshwater species through the Habitats Directive (HD, 92/43/EEC) and the Water Framework Directive (WFD, 2000/60/EC), and the eradication of Invasive Alien Species (IAS) through the Regulation 1143/2014. Periodic monitoring and reporting on the species listed in these regulations are mandatory for EU Member States.

pmc-13323753.title: Techno-economic and policy analysis of solar-wind powered EV charging for sustainable E-mobility
pmc-13323753.creator: Amit Kumar Yadav, Vedant Singh, Vibha Yadav, Rohit Khargotra, Tej Singh
pmc-13323753.description: In this study, the techno-economic viability of electric vehicle charging stations using a combination of solar photovoltaic and wind turbine technologies is examined, with specific reference to identifying the optimal configuration of wind turbine, solar photovoltaic, battery, and power conversion equipment. The cost of energy, net present cost, and initial capital cost are examined in varying climatic conditions in India.

pmc-13417395.title: Comparative Performance Assessment of Fiber Bragg Grating Sensors and PCB Accelerometers for Field-Based Dynamic Characterization of Stay Cables
pmc-13417395.creator: Do Hong Phuc, Ly Hoang Mai, Phi Van Toan, Lien Thi Ngoc Truong, Le Van Vu, Nguyen Thi Cam Nhung
pmc-13417395.description: Stay cables are critical components of cable-stayed bridges, and their dynamic characteristics provide essential information for vibration assessment and structural health monitoring. This study presents a comparative performance assessment of Fiber Bragg Grating (FBG) sensors and PCB accelerometers for field-based dynamic characterization of stay cables.

pmc-13568981.title: From Bonds to Barriers: Amphiphilic Molecules Enable Dual Interfacial and Electrolyte Regulation for Highly Stable Aqueous Zinc‐Ion Batteries
pmc-13568981.creator: Min Li, Chao Li, Lei Jiang, Xin Tan, Kwok‐Ho Lam, Qiaoji Zheng, Dunmin Lin
pmc-13568981.description: The uncontrolled growth of zinc dendrites and severe parasitic side reactions critically impede the practical development of aqueous zinc‐ion batteries (AZIBs), largely due to the high activity of water molecules in aqueous electrolytes. Herein, we report arbutin (HQOGP) as a green and multifunctional electrolyte additive capable of simultaneously stabilizing the electrolyte and zinc anode interface.

pmc-13571745.title: Artificial Intelligence in Particle Therapy Treatment Planning: Current Advances and Future Directions
pmc-13571745.creator: James CL Chow, Huan Giap
pmc-13571745.description: PurposeThis review examines the role of artificial intelligence (AI) in particle therapy treatment planning, highlighting recent advancements, clinical potential, and existing challenges.Methods and MaterialsA review was conducted on AI applications in proton and heavy ion therapy, focusing on automated plan generation, dose prediction, treatment adaptation, and quality assurance.

pmc-13643626.title: Clinically relevant intra‐articular corticosteroid doses impair equine osteoclast function in vitro
pmc-13643626.creator: Gwladys Malek, Louis Kamus, Hélène Richard, Guy Beauchamp, Sheila Laverty
pmc-13643626.description: ObjectiveTo assess the effects of clinically relevant doses of commonly employed intra‐articular corticosteroids—specifically, triamcinolone acetonide (TCA), methylprednisolone acetate (MPA), and combination of betamethasone acetate and betamethasone sodium phosphate (BM)—on equine osteoclasts.Study designIn vitro controlled laboratory study.Sample populationThree donor mares (13–19 years).
